title: Japan Leads OECD in Reading, Math and Science
paragraphs: Japanese students have achieved a historic result in one of the world's most important international tests. According to the latest results of the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), Japan ranked first among the 38 member countries of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) in all three subjects: reading, mathematics and science. It was the first time Japan had achieved this.
PISA is run by the OECD and tests the skills of 15-year-old students. The 2025 test, whose results were released in September 2026, was taken by about 760,000 students in 91 countries and regions.

Japan's average score was 503 points in reading, 536 in mathematics and 538 in science. When all participating countries and regions were included, Japan ranked fourth in reading and fifth in both mathematics and science. The top performers overall included Singapore and the Chinese areas of Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

However, the results were not entirely positive. Japan's scores actually fell compared with the previous test in 2022, by 13 points in reading, 11 points in mathematics and nine points in science. According to the OECD, Japan's results in mathematics and science stayed about the same, while its reading score declined. Japan was able to take first place partly because scores across OECD countries have been falling. In fact, the OECD reported that average performance in its member countries reached the lowest levels ever recorded in all three subjects.
In addition, the share of low-performing Japanese students rose in all three subjects. Students from families with more advantages were also more likely to achieve high scores.

The survey also raised concerns about students' attitudes. Fewer Japanese students than the OECD average said they enjoyed learning new things or felt strong curiosity. Japanese students were also less likely to plan how they study and change their approach when facing difficulties.
Japan also ranked last among OECD countries in the use of generative AI for studying. Only 7.0% of Japanese students used it every day or almost every day, compared with an OECD average of 19.1%.
On a more positive note, Japanese students spent less time on social media and videos on weekdays than students in other countries surveyed.
